introduction: This foundational level covers the most frequently tested Latin maxims that form the absolute baseline of Natural Justice, Criminal Law, and Contract Law. These phrases are the DNA of legal reasoning.

core_concepts.title: Audi Alteram Partem
core_concepts.description:
Meaning: 'Hear the other side' or 'No man shall be condemned unheard'.
- Application: The most fundamental rule of Natural Justice. It mandates that a decision-maker must give a fair opportunity to both parties to present their case and defend themselves before passing any adverse order.

core_concepts.title: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
core_concepts.description:
Meaning: 'An act does not make a person guilty unless the mind is also guilty'.
- Application: The foundation of Criminal Law. For a crime to occur, two elements must coexist: *Actus Reus* (the guilty physical act) and *Mens Rea* (the guilty mental intention). (e.g., Accidentally taking someone's umbrella thinking it's yours is not theft because there is no *mens rea*).

core_concepts.title: Ignorantia facti excusat, Ignorantia juris non excusat
core_concepts.description:
Meaning: 'Ignorance of fact is an excuse, ignorance of law is not an excuse'.
- Application: Embodied in Sections 76 and 79 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). If you commit an offense because you genuinely misunderstood a factual situation, you may be excused. However, you can NEVER claim 'I didn't know this was illegal' to escape liability. Every person is presumed to know the law of the land.

core_concepts.title: Caveat Emptor
core_concepts.description:
Meaning: 'Let the buyer beware'.
- Application: A core principle of the Sale of Goods Act (Section 16). It states that the seller is not obligated to point out defects in their goods. It is the buyer's duty to inspect the goods and ensure they are fit for their intended purpose before buying.

important_entities.name: Nemo judex in causa sua
important_entities.significance: Meaning: 'No one should be a judge in his own cause'. Along with *Audi Alteram Partem*, this forms the twin pillars of Natural Justice. It ensures that the adjudicator is completely impartial and has no personal, pecuniary (financial), or subject-matter interest in the dispute.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'Does the maxim *Ignorantia juris non excusat* apply to foreign law?' **NO**. Ignorance of domestic (Indian) law is no excuse. However, ignorance of a *foreign* law is legally treated as an ignorance of *fact*, and can therefore be used as a valid excuse under the Indian Contract Act (Section 21).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use these root words to instantly distinguish the two primary rules of administrative fairness.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'Which maxim forms the basis of Section 76 of the IPC?', select **Ignorantia facti excusat**.
